title: fix(app-shell,core): the Studio action editor stops offering aria, which the spec retired, and the runner drops its dead aria mirror (objectui#10929)
body:
Fixes #10929
Clause-②: no (narrowing)

`@objectstack/spec` 17.5.0 retired `action.aria` as a `retiredKey()` tombstone (objectstack PR 20398). This PR does the two things the card asks for, at objectui `main` `18d1a0abd`, which resolves `@objectstack/*` 17.5.0.

## 1. Studio action editor: measured first, and no `RETIRED_FIELDS` row

Zone 1 asked for a measurement before any code: does the served `action` schema drop the tombstone by itself?

**The served payload, from the published code.** I installed `@objectstack/metadata-protocol@17.5.0` from npm in a scratch directory. I called its own `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation.prototype.getMetaTypes()`, with `listLiveMetadataTypes` answering `['action']`. That is the function behind `GET /meta/types`, not a re-implementation of it.

| reading | result |
|---|---|
| served `action` schema, 17.5.0 | 44 properties; `aria`, `bulkEnabled` and `shortcut` absent; `label` and `variant` present (controls) |
| raw `z.toJSONSchema(ActionSchema, { unrepresentable: 'any', io: 'input' })`, same spec | `aria` present as `{ description: '[REMOVED] …', not: {} }` |
| `ActionSchema.safeParse` with an `aria` block | refused at `aria`, `invalid_type` |
| `acceptsNothing` occurrences in the published `metadata-protocol` dist: 17.3.0 / 17.4.0 / 17.5.0 | 0 / 0 / 2 (the strip first ships in 17.5.0) |
| served `action` schema, 17.4.0 (same probe) | a husk: only `$schema`, 0 properties |

**Through the real `ActionDefaultInspector`.** I ran a throwaway probe test (never committed) that mounts the inspector with each schema as `serverSchema`:

| schema fed to the inspector | draft | `aria` control offered | `order` row (control) |
|---|---|---|---|
| served 17.5.0 payload | plain | no | yes |
| served 17.5.0 payload | stores an `aria` block | no | yes |
| raw `io: 'input'` derivation (no strip) | plain | **yes** (`#mdf-aria`) | yes |

So the served schema drops `aria` structurally, and the "More fields" form stops offering it by itself. Per the ruling, **no `RETIRED_FIELDS` row is added** and `ActionDefaultInspector.tsx` is unchanged. A 17.4.0 server cannot put the control back either, because its served `action` schema has no properties at all. Servers older than 17.4.0 were not measured; `aria` was still authorable there, so offering it there was correct.

**The pin:** `ActionDefaultInspector.ariaRetired-10929.test.tsx`

- Its fixture comes from the installed spec with the call `/meta/types` uses for `action`, plus the served strip reproduced at top level: a non-required `{ not: {} }` property is dropped. objectui does not install `metadata-protocol`. The same probe checked the reproduction against the authentic payload: top-level key sets 44 = 44, no key only on one side. The strip dropped `execute`, `shortcut`, `bulkEnabled` and `aria`.
- Case 1: fed the served schema, the editor offers no `aria` control. The detector looks for a "More fields" host id and for any control whose accessible name says aria. Firing controls: the same detector finds the served `order` row and the curated `Label` control.
- Case 2: an action that already stores `aria: { ariaLabel, role }` opens without throwing. **What it shows:** the action as usual. The Label field reads `Approve`, the "More fields" rows render, and nothing names `aria`. `SchemaForm` builds rows from the schema's properties, never from keys only the value carries.

## 2. `ActionRunner`: the dead mirror is removed

- `ActionDef` loses `aria?: SpecActionInput['aria']`. At 17.5.0 that type is `undefined`.
- `ACTION_DEF_KEYS` loses its `aria` entry. `actionKeys.pin.test.ts` re-derives that list from the interface's AST, so the two have to move together.
- `aria` stays in `SPEC_ACTION_KEYS`, because `ActionSchema` still declares the tombstone. `KNOWN_ACTION_KEYS` is therefore unchanged, and so is the dev-mode unknown-key warning.
- `actionKeys.types.test.ts`: the `aria` row now compiles `{ aria: { ariaLabel: 'Approve' } }`, the shape that was valid before 17.5.0. It is rejected against `ActionDef` and clean against the index-signature control.

**No reader breaks.** `ActionDef` has no index signature, so any reader of `.aria` on it would now fail to compile. `@object-ui/core` type-check (both programs) is green. `@object-ui/app-shell` type-check is green against its rebuilt closure (29 packages). Building that closure also compiled every package in it against the new `ActionDef`.

**Reverse check: the consumer reads the rebuilt `.d.ts`.** I planted a temporary `packages/app-shell/src/__revcheck10929.ts` and ran app-shell `tsc --noEmit`:

- `{ name: 'x', aria: undefined }` gave `TS2353: Object literal may only specify known properties, and 'aria' does not exist in type 'ActionDef'`. The old `aria?: undefined` accepts that literal, so this discriminates old from new.
- The control line `{ name: 'x', ai: undefined }` was clean.
- The file was removed by a trap, and `git status` was clean afterwards.
- The rebuilt `packages/core/dist/actions/ActionRunner.d.ts` has no `aria` member in `ActionDef`. Its `ai`, `bodyExtra`, `shortcut` and `bulkEnabled` members are present.

## Ablation (run from committed `b70c10a4d`, through `ablation-replace.mjs`, restore proven by blob == HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`)

- **Leg A, re-add the control.** An `InspectorTextField` labelled `ARIA label`, writing `aria`, is planted in the inspector's Behavior section. The on-disk marker count was 1. Run over the 12 test files that reference `ActionDefaultInspector`: `Test Files 1 failed | 11 passed (12)`, `Tests 2 failed | 116 passed (118)`. The 2 failures are exactly the two new pins. The first attempt was a no-op: the tool refused it because the replacement contained its own anchor, and it restored the file. That run is not counted.
- **Leg B, the served strip skipped in the fixture.** Only the new file was run: `Tests 2 failed (2)`, both on `#mdf-aria`. The detector sees the "More fields" row path as well as a curated control.

- `pnpm exec vitest run` over `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/` in three chunks:
  - 40 files, 415 passed
  - 40 files, 393 passed
  - 39 files, 833 passed and 1 skipped
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/core type-check`: exit 0
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check`: exit 0, after building its closure (core and types first, then two more tiers)
- `pnpm exec eslint` on the 4 changed source/test files: 0 errors. The 20 warnings are existing `no-explicit-any` in `ActionRunner.ts`.
- These checks all exited 0:
  - `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`
  - `check-control-bytes`
  - `check-new-cross-file-line-citations` (0 new)
  - `check-installed-spec-pin-claims`
  - `check-action-forward-parity`
  - `check-changeset-claims`
  - `check-pending-changeset-literals`
  - `check-changeset-no-major`
  - `check-test-path-roots`
  - the three `check-vi-mock-*` gates
- The changeset is markdown, so I also ran `node scripts/markdown-test-inputs.mjs --audit` (exit 0) and `pnpm exec vitest run scripts/__tests__/`: `Test Files 177 passed | 2 skipped (179)`, `Tests 5371 passed | 2 skipped`.
- Declared narrowing: the type-check sweep covers `@object-ui/core` and the app-shell closure. The other downstream consumers of `@object-ui/core` (`...@object-ui/core`) are CI's `type-check`, as is the repo-wide `pnpm lint`.

## Acceptance notes (observations, not filed)

- **The `bulkEnabled` / `shortcut` rows of `RETIRED_FIELDS` hide nothing against any published server.** Their comment says the served schema "still advertises both". Measured above, 17.4.0 serves `action` with 0 properties, and 17.5.0 strips both tombstones. So the premise holds at neither release. Untouched here: the ruling rules out `RETIRED_FIELDS` edits on this card. Nobody is carrying it.
- **From 17.5.0 the "More fields" section offers 22 non-curated keys for the first time.** Before, the served `action` schema was a husk. Among the 22 are the seven package-lock provenance stamps: `_lock`, `_lockReason`, `_lockSource`, `_lockDocsUrl`, `_provenance`, `_packageId`, `_packageVersion`. This list is the served key set minus the curated and hidden lists. I did not check rendering key by key, and did not measure what Save does with an edited stamp. Nobody is carrying it.
- **A stored `aria` block is neither shown nor stripped by the editor.** By reading `SchemaForm`'s `setField`, a "More fields" edit re-emits the whole draft, so the block rides along to Save. What the save door does with it is NOT MEASURED. The card says the ADR-0087 conversion `action-aria-removed` strips it from stored rows.
